# Disney (DIS) — Quantitative Fundamental Attractiveness Report
**Decision date: 2026-04-24**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margin, and Cash-Flow Trajectory

Disney's latest quarter (Q1 FY2026, period_end 2025-12-27) delivered revenue of $25.98B, up 5.2% YoY from the prior-year Q1 ($24.69B, 2024-12-28). Sequentially, revenue jumped 9.9% from Q3 ($23.65B, 2025-06-28). However, the earnings picture diverges sharply: diluted EPS of $1.34 declined 4.3% YoY and plunged 54.1% QoQ from Q3's $2.92. Net income fell to $2.48B from $2.64B a year earlier (−6.1% YoY) and from $5.94B in Q3 (−58.2% QoQ). Revenue growth outpaced earnings growth, signaling margin erosion in the latest period.

Operating income was $4.60B versus $5.06B in Q1 a year prior (−9.1% YoY), despite $1.29B more in revenue. Operating margin compressed to ~17.7% (calculated from the income statement) from ~20.5% in Q1 FY2025, though the supplied operating_margin ratio of 0.179 suggests the decline may partly reflect quarter-to-quarter variability rather than structural degradation.

Operating cash flow collapsed to $735M in the latest quarter — down 77.1% YoY from $3.21B and down 80.0% QoQ from $3.67B in Q3. This is the weakest OCF quarter in the four-quarter window. Free cash flow is unavailable. Missing FCF does not negate the concern: $735M of OCF on $25.98B of revenue implies heavy near-term cash absorption (likely working capital, capex timing, or both).

**Important caveat:** The supplied quarters are [Q1 FY2026, Q3 FY2025, Q2 FY2025, Q1 FY2025] — with a fiscal gap (Q4 FY2025 is absent). TTM totals cannot be computed; no trailing-twelve-month aggregate is cited below.

## 2. Earnings Quality and Balance-Sheet Resilience

**Earnings quality:** The disconnect between revenue growth (+5.2% YoY) and earnings decline (−4.3% YoY) in Q1 FY2026 warrants scrutiny. The Q3 FY2025 figure ($2.92 EPS, $5.94B net income) may include non-recurring items — net income of $5.94B on $23.65B revenue implies a net margin of ~25.1%, far above the 13.9% trailing ratio. Excluding Q3, the other three quarters show more consistent net margins in the 9.5–14.4% range. The sudden QoQ EPS decline from $2.92 to $1.34 likely reflects normalization from Q3's elevated level rather than a fresh deterioration, though the YoY decline against a relatively ordinary Q1 is a yellow flag.

**Balance sheet:** Total equity expanded to $114.01B (2025-12-27) from $106.74B a year prior, a +6.8% YoY improvement. The debt-to-equity ratio (total_liabilities / total_equity) stands at 0.77x (88.08B / 114.01B), modestly improved from 0.85x a year ago (90.31B / 106.74B). Total assets grew to $202.09B. The balance sheet is resilient and de-levering, which provides cushion against the cash-flow volatility. ROE has improved to 11.6% from 5.9% one year prior — a near-doubling that reflects better earnings conversion on a growing equity base.

## 3. Valuation Versus Own History

At pe_diluted = 14.0x (2026-04-23), Disney trades at a sharp discount to its one-year range of 12.5x–26.8x. One year ago (2025-04-24), the multiple was 26.1x. The market has re-rated the stock downward from an expensive level to near the bottom of its historical range. This re-rating occurred even as net margin improved from 6.8% (2025-04-24) to 13.9% (2026-02-18), and ROE rose from 5.9% to 11.6%. P/B of 1.63x sits near the floor of the 1.5x–2.1x range. P/S of 1.94x is moderate.

The earnings yield of 7.1% compares favorably against the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.34% — a spread of ~276 bps — suggesting the stock compensates for the rate regime. The 2.42% 10-year breakeven inflation rate implies real yields near 1.92%, further supporting the relative case.

**However**, a low P/E alone is not "cheap" — it is cheap only if earnings are durable and quality. The Q1 cash-flow collapse and the YoY EPS decline introduce doubt about whether the 14x multiple accurately reflects normalized earnings power versus a quarter that may be tracking toward an earnings miss if the trend continues.

## 4. Price Context Versus Fundamentals

Price has declined 8.4% over the last ~63 trading days (from $113.21 on 2026-01-22 to $103.65 on 2026-04-23) and is down ~17% from the 52-week high of $124.69. The path has been persistent selling: −7.0% in Q3 2025, −1.0% in Q4 2025, −8.4% in Q1 2026. The price decline has roughly tracked the earnings and cash-flow disappointment — the market is not overshooting relative to the fundamental signal so far, though the compression in P/E from 26x to 14x without proportionate earnings improvement suggests sentiment has deteriorated faster than the business.

## 5. Macro and Sentiment Overlays

**Macro headwinds are material.** WTI crude has surged 64% over the window ($60.46 → $99.27), creating direct cost pressure for Disney's parks, cruise lines, and logistics. The 10-year yield at 4.34% and the Baa corporate spread at 6.02% elevate the cost of capital for a capital-intensive operator. VIX at 19.31 (up 19.6% over the quarter) signals elevated risk appetite uncertainty. The yield curve (T10Y2Y = 0.51%) remains positively sloped but has flattened from 0.66%, a mild tightening signal. Initial claims at 215K are stable — the labor market is not flashing recession. The oil shock is the most consequential macro variable for Disney's margin outlook.

**News sentiment** is modestly positive at a mean of 0.348 across 67 scored articles in the last 90 days. Sentiment is not extreme enough to override the fundamental picture in either direction.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside and Downside

**Upside drivers:**
- P/E at 14.0x is near the 12.5x floor of the one-year range; if Q1 weakness proves seasonal or transient, reversion toward the 17–22x range seen in mid-2025 implies 20–50% upside on stable earnings.
- ROE improvement from 5.9% to 11.6% over twelve months is a genuine operating transformation; continued margin normalization supports higher intrinsic value.
- Balance sheet de-leveraging (D/E from 0.85x to 0.77x) creates financial flexibility.

**Downside drivers:**
- OCF of $735M is deeply abnormal versus the prior three quarters ($3.21B–$6.75B); if Q1 FY2026 cash generation is the new baseline rather than an outlier, the equity story deteriorates sharply.
- Operating margin compression YoY (~20.5% → ~17.7%) combined with a 64% oil price shock creates a credible scenario for further margin erosion.
- The missing Q4 FY2025 quarter means the TTM picture is opaque — the market may be pricing information asymmetry.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

Disney presents a **moderately attractive** fundamental setup with meaningful caveats. The valuation re-rating from 26x to 14x P/E, concurrent with genuine profitability improvement (ROE doubling, margin recovery from the 2025 trough), creates a valuation mismatch. The balance sheet is healthy and de-levering. However, the latest quarter's OCF collapse to $735M, the YoY earnings decline, and the oil-driven margin headwind introduce real uncertainty about whether current earnings are sustainable or deteriorating. The market has not overreacted — price declines have tracked the fundamental softness. At 14x earnings with a 7.1% earnings yield versus 4.34% risk-free, the stock offers adequate compensation, but conviction requires visibility into Q4 FY2025 (missing) and confirmation that Q1's cash-flow weakness is transitory.

## Disney (DIS) — Qualitative Franchise Assessment

**Decision date:** 2026-04-24 | **Assessment:** Moderately Positive

---

### 1. Business / Franchise Read

Disney operates one of the most integrated IP-to-consumer monetization ecosystems in global entertainment. The structural narrative, drawn from multiple business-model analyses, describes a "flywheel" in which studio content (Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar, classic Disney) feeds recurring revenue across streaming (Disney+, Hulu), experiential consumption (12 theme parks globally, cruise lines), sports media (ESPN), and consumer products. Vertical control — from a film to a toy to a theme-park ticket — allows Disney to capture a larger share of lifetime consumer spend than any media peer.

**Experiences** is the franchise cornerstone. The segment generated $34.1 billion in FY2024 revenue with $9.3 billion in operating income (matrixbcg.com, 2026-04-23). In Q1 FY2026 it posted record quarterly revenue of $10 billion and record operating income of $3.3 billion (247wallst.com, 2026-04-21). Domestic parks pricing power remains intact, supported by premium offerings such as Lightning Lane Premier Pass and VIP experiences. A $60 billion multi-year capital plan for parks and cruise expansion (new ships Disney Destiny and Disney Adventure; World of Frozen at Disneyland Paris; proposed Abu Dhabi park) signals management conviction in long-duration experiential demand.

**Direct-to-Consumer (DTC)** streaming has pivoted from subscriber-growth-at-all-costs to profitability. DTC reported quarterly operating income of $321 million by end of 2024; by Q1 FY2026, streaming operating income surged 72% year-over-year to $450 million (matrixbcg.com, 2026-04-23; 247wallst.com, 2026-04-21). Ad-supported tiers and anti-password-sharing measures are lifting ARPU. Hulu's full integration into Disney+ in the US simplifies the bundle and reduces churn. Disney+ globally exceeded 130 million subscribers in 2025 across legacy groupings (matrixbcg.com, 2026-04-23).

**ESPN** maintains dual affiliate/advertising revenue while transitioning toward a flagship DTC sports service by late 2025–2026. Management projects materially higher DTC ARPU if live sports can be monetized outside traditional MVPD packages.

A $7.5 billion cost-reduction program, $3 billion share-buyback authorization in FY2024, reinstated dividends, and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.43–0.48 (investopedia.com, 2026-04-14) indicate a shift toward shareholder-friendly capital allocation and balance-sheet discipline. FY2024 revenue totaled $91.4 billion with $15.6 billion in segment operating income. Management projects double-digit adjusted EPS growth into 2026.

---

### 2. Dated Recent Developments

- **2026-04-18 (news):** Motley Fool article noted YouTube has become the world's largest streaming platform with $60B+ revenue — a competitive data point highlighting how tech platforms are scaling in Disney's content-distribution arena.

- **2026-04-15 (news):** Disney cut approximately 1,000 jobs across media divisions, with Marvel Studios among the hardest hit. Affected roles span visual development, production, and support in New York and Burbank. Some artists are being shifted to contract-based roles. This signals a deliberate reduction of Marvel's production slate — an inference is that management is prioritizing quality over volume in franchise output, which could improve per-title economics but near-term constrains content volume.

- **2026-04-14 (news):** A detailed analysis of Disney's "$60 billion secret weapon" — the "Human Bridge" cultural-localization strategy — highlighted that Shanghai Disney Resort reached 100 million guests, and that this model (building institutional trust through local partnerships rather than exporting Western IP wholesale) is being replicated for the Singapore Disney Adventure cruise ship and the proposed Abu Dhabi Disneyland. The analysis noted that rising "war risk" insurance premiums in the Middle East introduce new variables for the Abu Dhabi project.

- **2026-04-13 (news):** Survey data showed 36% of Americans would accept twice as many ads for cheaper streaming (49% of Gen Z), indicating the ad-tier opportunity is real and consumer willingness exists — supportive of Disney's ad-supported tier monetization strategy.

- **2026-04-11 (news):** Motley Fool flagged Disney stock down 50% over five years and 16% YTD in 2026, with a forward P/E of 14.4 — a 29% discount to the S&P 500. Streaming operating income up 72% YoY and Experiences at 28% operating margins were cited as reasons to buy the dip.

- **2026-04-11 (news):** Nintendo's expanding entertainment ambitions (Super Mario Galaxy Movie on track for $1B+ gross, annual movie releases, theme park expansion) represent a credible new competitive vector in family-friendly content and IP-to-experience monetization, though Disney's franchise depth remains substantially broader.

- **Q2 FY2026 preview (updates):** Earnings expected May 6, 2026. Consensus EPS: $1.49 (+2.8% YoY). Full-year FY2026 consensus EPS: $6.61 (+11.5% from FY2025's $5.93). Disney has beaten EPS estimates in the last four consecutive quarters.

- **Insider activity (updates):** Net insider selling of ~$460K over the past 12 months, including a $282K sale by the Chief People Officer in January 2026. Modest in absolute terms but directionally negative.

---

### 3. Material Qualitative Risks and Offsets

| Risk | Severity | Offset / Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Streaming competition & saturation** — Netflix ($418B mkt cap), Amazon, Apple competing aggressively; Disney+ subscriber additions lagging expectations | High | Ad tiers, Hulu bundle integration, ARPU focus, $7.5B cost program driving profitability even at slower sub growth |
| **Linear TV / cord-cutting** — ESPN traditional affiliate fees eroding | Medium-High | ESPN DTC transition underway; sports rights (NFL, NBA, college) provide live-viewing moat resistant to time-shifted disruption |
| **Marvel / franchise fatigue** — reduced slate, job cuts at Marvel Studios signal quality concerns | Medium | Management explicitly prioritizing quality over volume; Inside Out 2's $1.6B box office (2024) shows franchise IP can still deliver outsized returns when execution is strong |
| **Capital intensity** — $60B parks commitment over 10 years; $9B annual capex in FY2026 | Medium | Experiences segment generates >25% margins and record cash flow; $10B+ annual FCF historically; debt-to-equity of 0.43–0.48 preserves balance-sheet flexibility |
| **Macro / discretionary spending sensitivity** — parks and merchandise vulnerable to economic slowdowns | Medium | Experiences pricing power historically resilient; diversified revenue across segments; family travel remains a priority spend category |
| **Geopolitical & international park risk** — Abu Dhabi project faces elevated "war risk" insurance costs; international parks (Paris, Hong Kong) face currency and attendance volatility | Medium | "Human Bridge" localization strategy designed as a regulatory and demand hedge; domestic parks anchor profitability |
| **Regulatory / antitrust scrutiny** — Disney's dominance in kids' content and media consolidation draws attention | Low-Medium | Proactive governance reforms; ~63% institutional ownership aligned with compliance expectations |
| **Competitive disruption from gaming/interactive** — Nintendo, Tencent expanding into Disney's family-entertainment territory | Low-Medium | $1.5B Epic Games investment targets persistent digital worlds; broader IP ecosystem (parks, merchandise) creates switching costs competitors lack |

---

### 4. Qualitative Assessment

**The narrative supports fundamental attractiveness with qualifications.**

Disney possesses a genuinely durable franchise: unmatched IP breadth, a uniquely integrated content-to-experience flywheel, and a dominant position in theme parks with pricing power and >25% segment margins. The streaming business has inflected to profitability and is scaling ARPU through ad tiers and bundling. The $60B parks investment, while capital-intensive, extends the experiential growth runway well into the next decade. Balance-sheet discipline (0.43–0.48 D/E, reinstated dividends, $3B buyback) and a $7.5B cost program signal a management team focused on returns rather than growth-at-any-cost. The stock trades at a forward P/E of 14.4 — a 29% discount to the S&P 500 — which compresses a lot of execution concern into the price.

The qualifications are real: Marvel output is being curtailed (job cuts, reduced slate), subscriber growth is decelerating, linear TV is in secular decline, and the $60B parks commitment raises capital-allocation risk if macro softens. Nintendo's emergence as a credible competitor in family entertainment and IP-to-theme-park monetization is a structural headwind that did not exist five years ago. Insider selling, while modest, provides no confidence signal.

On balance, the franchise quality is high, the competitive moat is wide (IP library, integrated flywheel, pricing power in experiences), and structural growth vectors exist (streaming profitability ramp, parks expansion, ESPN DTC, gaming via Epic Games). The valuation discount appears to price in more risk than the franchise warrants, making the qualitative narrative modestly supportive of fundamental attractiveness. Execution on Marvel quality, ESPN DTC transition, and streaming ARPU will determine whether the discount narrows.

---
